name: Southeast Buttress (South Peak)
pitch_detail: The route climbs a divided buttress. The more prominent eastern portion is a 700-ft lower east buttress gained via diagonally-cutting bench systems, leading to a vertical headwall bounded on its right by a sheer east face. Above that, the account describes a steep, loose 5.6 chimney, an 80-foot, 50-degree dihedral, and a 4th-class chimney, followed by roughly 200 feet of scrambling to the summit. Most of the roped climbing besides the 5.6 chimney is described as 4th class.
approach: From the Lightning Creek trailhead on Ross Lake, the first-ascent party hiked east past Willow Lake, then left the trail to bushwhack through timber and avalanche debris, crossed a ravine, and climbed steep dirt and brush to open timber on the broad shoulder south of the peak. They reached meadows near 5,000 ft and bypassed cliff bands to a saddle at about 6,200 ft below the buttress — roughly six hours from the trailhead — where they bivouacked.
overview: A Grade III, 5.6 technical rock route on the South Peak's southeast side.
fa: Dave Adams, Don Goodman, Ken Johnson, and John Petroske, June 25-26, 1988
